event: Sunday: you wake before dawn in Bea's bed in 15, her bare arm over you, her face in your hair.
You ease out from under her arm; she stirs. "Rock?" she mumbles. "Sunday. Go on. Shiv's waiting."
You kiss her shoulder, find your clothes in the dark, and leave a note on her pillow: Back by ten.
The rock in the grey light: Shiv is already there in her parka, sitting very still, looking out.
She turns when your feet crunch on the shingle; she grins, but it comes slow this morning.
"Sunday," she says. "No register. No whistle. Just us and the fells." You strip, shivering.
You jump off the rock together, hand in hand, the way you did the first time, into the black water.
The cold takes your breath; you come up breathing out; Shiv floats on her back, eyes on the sky.
You swim out farther than the buoy would let you, just the two of you, and back to the rock.
On the rock after, wrapped in the parka together, Shiv is quiet a long time; you let her be.
"My mam swam the sea at Salthill every morning of her life," Shiv says. "Winter too. Every day."

memory.fact: Shiv's mother swam the sea at Salthill every morning of her life, winter too, and taught Shiv there.

event: "She taught me there. I was four. She threw me in off the steps and said: kick, Siobhan."

memory.fact: At four Shiv's mam threw her in off the Salthill steps and shouted: kick, Siobhan.

pictured.coverAfter: On the rock after, you sit wrapped in the parka together.
pictured.outfit: navy parka over bare skin, wet hair, bare legs

event: She laughs, and the laugh goes thin. "She died last winter. January. I came here on what she left."

memory.fact: Shiv's mother died last winter, and Shiv came to Hollowmere on the money she left.

event: You look at her; this is new to you. You put your hand over hers on the cold stone.
"Every dawn I go in," Shiv says, "it's her. That's all it is. It's swimming with her."

memory.fact: Shiv says every dawn swim off her rock is swimming with her mam; that's all it's ever been.

event: "The register," she says. "Being counted. She never signed a thing in her life. She just went in."
Shiv cries then, suddenly, hard, her face in her hands; the first time in front of anyone, she says.
You hold her inside the parka, her wet hair against your cheek, while the light comes up pink.

memory.fact: Shiv cried hard on the rock in Nala's arms, the first time in front of anyone since her mam died.
Shiv cried hard on the rock in Nala's arms, the first time in front of anyone since her mam died.

event: When it passes she wipes her face on her sleeve. "Christ. Sorry. You came for a swim."
"I came for you," you say. Shiv looks at you a long moment, and her crooked grin comes back.
She studies your face. "You've a look on you," she says. "Lindqvist?" You go pink. You nod.
Shiv laughs, properly now. "Good. About time. She's been mad for you since the first morning."

memory.fact: Reading Nala's face, Shiv guessed Lindqvist, and said Bea's been mad for her since the first day.
Reading Nala's face, Shiv guessed Lindqvist, and said Bea's been mad for her since the first day.

event: "And you?" you ask. Shiv shrugs inside the parka. "I want you too, Ashby. You know I do."
"When it's right," she says. "I'm in no hurry. I've a whole year of Sundays." She kisses you, salt.

memory.fact: Shiv told Nala she wants her too, when it's right; she's in no hurry, with a whole year of Sundays.
Shiv told Nala she wants her too, when it's right; she's in no hurry, with a whole year of Sundays.

event: You walk back up to Thornfield at nine; Bea is awake in 15 with tea, and she reads your face.
"Shiv's all right?" You tell her a little; Bea goes quiet, then says she'll be kind to her today.

memory.fact: Shiv's mother died last winter, and Shiv came to Hollowmere on the money she left.
Shiv's mother swam the sea at Salthill every morning of her life, winter too, and taught Shiv there.

event: The Sunday roast at one: the whole crowd at one table, Kit, Lin, Priya, Amara too, for once.
Bea sits beside Shiv and fills her plate without asking, extra potatoes; Shiv lets her.

memory.fact: Told of Shiv's mam, Bea said she'd be kind to Shiv today; at roast she filled Shiv's plate unasked.
Told of Shiv's mam, Bea said she'd be kind to Shiv today; at roast she filled Shiv's plate unasked.
Told of Shiv's mam, Bea said she'd be kind to Shiv today; at roast she filled Shiv's plate unasked.

event: Kit, opposite, sees Bea's hand rest on your knee under the table, and you see her see it.
After the meal Kit falls into step with you in the cloister. "Lindqvist," she says. Not a question.
You say yes, last night. Kit walks a few steps in silence, then: "Good. She's decent. She said so."
"Are you all right?" you ask. Kit considers it. "Yes," she says, surprised. "I find I am."

memory.fact: Told Nala and Bea began last night, Kit said: Good, she's decent. All right? I find I am.
Told Nala and Bea began last night, Kit said: Good, she's decent. All right? I find I am.

pictured.coverAfter: After the meal, Kit falls into step with you in the cloister.

event: "Library," Kit says. "Tonight. Seven. You still owe me an hour of silence." Her ears are pink.
Afternoon: the boathouse lends rowing boats on Sundays; Shiv wants to go out, and asks you.
Shiv rows; you sit in the stern; she takes you out to the middle of the mere and ships the oars.
You drift. Shiv lies back in the bottom of the boat with her head on a lifejacket, eyes closed.
She sings under her breath, one of her mam's songs, Irish, and you lie back too and listen.
The boat turns slowly in the middle of the mere; the fells go round you, gold in the low sun.
"She'd have liked you," Shiv says, eyes still shut. "She'd have said you're too thin. Feed you."

memory.fact: Adrift on the mere, Shiv sang Nala one of her mam's Irish songs: she'd have liked you, she said.
Adrift on the mere, Shiv sang Nala one of her mam's Irish songs: she'd have liked you, she said.

event: You row back, badly, in circles; Shiv laughs at you so hard she nearly goes over the side.

memory.fact: Rowing Shiv back across the mere, Nala went in circles, and Shiv nearly laughed herself overboard.
Rowing Shiv back across the mere, Nala went in circles, and Shiv nearly laughed herself overboard.

event: Seven: the library reading room, green lamps, the long oak table; Kit has moved her books for you.
You work an hour in silence beside her, your Sigils notes open; her foot rests against yours.
At eight she writes on your page: Monday's practical. I'll take a middle bench. Watched. Ish.
You write back: I know. She folds your note very small, and keeps it, and goes back to her book.

memory.fact: Kit wrote Nala: Monday's practical, a middle bench. Watched. Ish. She kept Nala's reply: I know.

event: At nine you walk with Shiv to the Drowned Bell; it's quiet on a Sunday, the fire low.
Shiv puts a coin in the old jukebox and plays the one Pogues record, the way she does every night.
"Her song," Shiv says. "She'd sing it doing the dishes. Every night." She sits, and listens.

memory.fact: The Pogues song Shiv plays every night was her mam's, sung doing the dishes every night.

event: You sit with her by the fire with half a cider each while it plays, and then once more.
Walking home along the black shore, Shiv takes your hand and swings it. "Next Sunday," she says.
At Thornfield's door she kisses you goodnight, slow and salt, and goes off whistling the song.
Upstairs, Bea's door is ajar, the lamp on; she lifts the covers, silent, smiling, and you get in.
You fall asleep in 15 with Bea warm at your back and the Pogues still going round in your head.
